# `generator-shortcuts`

The strongest plausible shortcut is:

> Treat header values `1,2,3` as ranks of the source blocks’ foreground colors
> in ascending color order, rather than as the blocks’ top-to-bottom source
> positions.

It fits all three usable canonical demonstrations because their source-block
colors increase with source position. I checked this by executing the retained
`CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS["header_values_as_color_ranks"]` function on every
canonical pair; the fit vector is `[true, true, true]` in
`checks/shortcut-counterexample/record.json`.

## Exact disagreeing input

This input is emitted by generator v3.0.0 with seed `19`, sample index `1`, and
exact overrides `block_h=3`, `block_w=7`, `permutation="213"`,
`palette_profile="varied"`:

```json
[[2,6,6,0,0,0,6,6],
 [1,6,0,6,6,6,0,0],
 [3,0,6,0,6,0,0,0],
 [0,4,0,0,0,4,0,0],
 [0,4,0,0,4,0,4,0],
 [0,0,0,0,0,4,0,4],
 [0,0,2,0,0,2,2,2],
 [0,0,0,0,0,0,2,0],
 [0,2,0,0,0,0,0,0]]
```

The header is `2,1,3`, while the source colors by top-to-bottom position are
`6,4,2`. The intended positional rule therefore outputs block colors in order
`4,6,2`:

```json
[[4,0,0,0,4,0,0],
 [4,0,0,4,0,4,0],
 [0,0,0,0,4,0,4],
 [6,6,0,0,0,6,6],
 [6,0,6,6,6,0,0],
 [0,6,0,6,0,0,0],
 [0,2,0,0,2,2,2],
 [0,0,0,0,0,2,0],
 [2,0,0,0,0,0,0]]
```

The color-rank shortcut interprets header `2,1,3` as middle-, lowest-, then
highest-ranked color and predicts colors `4,2,6` instead:

```json
[[4,0,0,0,4,0,0],
 [4,0,0,4,0,4,0],
 [0,0,0,0,4,0,4],
 [0,2,0,0,2,2,2],
 [0,0,0,0,0,2,0],
 [2,0,0,0,0,0,0],
 [6,6,0,0,0,6,6],
 [6,0,6,6,6,0,0],
 [0,6,0,6,0,0,0]]
```

I obtained the intended output with the supported canonical-authority command
recorded in `checks/shortcut-counterexample/racket.json`; it executed rule hash
`7f09fab6403a`, accepted the input, and matched the independent Python mirror.
The rival output differs. The proposed generator not only emits this exact case,
but schedules a non-monotone `varied` palette in every three-sample ordinary
lesson window. The 300-lesson census found the shortcut refuted in 100/100
lessons in each difficulty band.
